"""The F5 distinguishing carrier: one qualname, several signatures.

Every public symbol here exists to separate a key that reads the SYMBOL
alone from the ratified ``(SYMBOL, canonical_signature_variant)``:

* ``render`` is declared three times — two ``@overload`` stubs plus the
  implementation.  All three share ``pkg.api_overloads:render``, so a
  SYMBOL-only key names one entity where the producer emitted three, and
  only the signature tells them apart.
* ``Renderer.emit`` repeats the same shape one level down, inside a class,
  so the method path is distinguished too and not only the module path.
* ``describe`` is a lone public function: the neighbour that proves the
  key still names a single row when nothing overloads it.

The module is deliberately trivial otherwise: no clone-sized bodies, no
security surfaces, no cycles — the stage measures the api_surface lane and
the families that ride every run, nothing else.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import overload

__all__ = ["Renderer", "describe", "render"]


@overload
def render(value: int) -> str: ...


@overload
def render(value: str, *, upper: bool = False) -> str: ...


def render(value: int | str, *, upper: bool = False) -> str:
    """Render one value; the implementation behind the two stubs."""
    text = str(value)
    return text.upper() if upper else text


def describe(value: object) -> str:
    """A single-declaration public function — the unambiguous neighbour."""
    return type(value).__name__


class Renderer:
    """A public class whose method carries the same overload shape."""

    @overload
    def emit(self, value: int) -> str: ...

    @overload
    def emit(self, value: str, *, upper: bool = False) -> str: ...

    def emit(self, value: int | str, *, upper: bool = False) -> str:
        """Emit one value; the implementation behind the two stubs."""
        return render(value, upper=upper)
